diagram_math_checks.details: M is a right R-module, N an (R,S)-bimodule, P a left S-module. L=(M⊗_R N)⊗_S P is typed using the right S-action on M⊗_R N, and T=M⊗_R(N⊗_S P) using the left R-action on N⊗_S P, exactly as local [L1] and its supplier state. The top vertex is a set of triples; q_L and q_T are explicitly set maps, not claimed homomorphisms from the product.
q_L(mr,n,p)=((mr)⊗n)⊗p=(m⊗rn)⊗p=q_L(m,rn,p). For q_T, (mr)⊗(n⊗p)=m⊗r(n⊗p)=m⊗((rn)⊗p), using the outer action in [L1]. These are the relations used in proof steps 1.1 and 2.2.

q_L(m,ns,p)=(m⊗ns)⊗p=((m⊗n)s)⊗p=(m⊗n)⊗sp; q_T(m,ns,p)=m⊗((ns)⊗p)=m⊗(n⊗sp). The commuting R/S actions on N ensure both induced outer actions are well-defined; this is precisely the bimodule-action supplier and proof steps 1.2 and 2.1.

The displayed α:L→T takes ((m⊗n)⊗p) to m⊗(n⊗p), and β:T→L reverses that formula. Consequently α q_L=q_T and β q_T=q_L for every triple, by proof steps 2.1 and 2.2; no unlabeled extra coherence relation is asserted.

β α=id_L and α β=id_T follow from equality on elementary tensors, which generate the groups, as in step 3.1. If M has a compatible additional left A-action and P a compatible right B-action, both composites send a and b to ((am)⊗n)⊗(pb) in L, or (am)⊗(n⊗(pb)) in T; hence the two arrows respect those outer actions as in step 3.2. The illustration does not assert an action without those hypotheses.
No existing proof text changed; the complete original argument ends before Remarks and derives the isomorphism, inverse, outer-action compatibility and naturality independently of the diagram.
